newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Great Eastern $50 mln FRN closed.
newsitem.headline: India's Great Eastern $50 mln FRN closed.

text.p: India's Great Eastern Shipping Company Ltd successfully concluded a $50 million floating rate note (FRN) issue, lead manager ANZ Grindlays Bank said on Tuesday.

"The issue was priced at 135 basis points over the six-month LIBOR with a reoffer price of 99.85 percent to give a discounted margin of 138 basis points over LIBOR to the investors," the bank said in a statement.
ANZ is the market maker for this paper and is committed to create an active market during its 7-year life, it said.
Great Eastern is India's largest private shipping company.
"This issue is also the first 7-year FRN to be issued by a private Indian corporate on an unsecured basis," it said.
The funds are to be used to expand Great Eastern's fleet.

"With this transaction, ANZ has clearly emerged as the market leader for lead and co-lead managing Indian bond/FRN issues, with over $920 million arranged since 1994," the statement quoted Rana Kapoor, ANZ general manager, as saying.
He said the deal was structured differently from normal shipping deals.
"Most shipping companies usually float paper for financing specific ship acquisitions, whilst here, investors get an opportunity to invest in the group's balance sheet."

"Whilst most Indian corporates are adopting the syndicated loan route for their offshore fund raising, we strategically decided on a capital market issue to develop a broad investor base," it quoted Ravi Sheth, Great Eastern's executive vice president, as saying.
